stimulus.text: Secondary passage written for this question. Maize was first grown in Mesoamerica, in what is now Mexico, thousands of years before Europeans arrived. Over time, maize farming spread north into the American Southwest and then into the river valleys of the Southeast and Midwest, and east into the Northeast woodlands. As maize spread, new towns and chiefdoms grew where farming could feed them. Trade networks carried maize seed, copper, shells, and stone across long distances, linking peoples who lived far apart.
stimulus.source_note: Original secondary passage written for this question, summarizing the grounding books and the Unit 1 lesson script.

parts.prompt: Identify one way the spread of maize changed Native societies in North America.
Explain how trade networks connected Native societies before European contact.
Explain one similarity between the Mississippian chiefdoms and the societies of Mesoamerica.

instruction: Answer each part in your own words from the stimulus only. Do not open the question file.
